summary: Alison Denton Jones works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Martin King Whyte as her doctoral supervisor, as well as under Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret H. Dornish.

Alka Patel specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed a bachelor's at Mount Holyoke College (c. 1985–1989) and a PhD at Harvard (c. 1993–2000), and became Associate Professor at UC Irvine around 2007.

Allan G. Grapard (1944–2025) was a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from INALCO. He held posts as ISF Professor of Shinto Studies at UC (c. 1989–2004) and Professor Emeritus at UC Santa Barbara.

Allan Gibbard is a philosopher who studied at Swarthmore (B.A. c. 1959–1963) and Harvard (Ph.D. c. 1965–1971). He held faculty positions at the University of Chicago (1969–1974), University of Pittsburgh (1974–1977), and University of Michigan (1977–2016).
Allan H. Barr is a sinologist who completed a doctorate at the University of Oxford by 1983. He was appointed Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College in 1981.

Allan Harrison Fry (1910–1979) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Princeton (A.B. c. 1928–1932) and the universities of Basel and Bonn (1935–1937). He taught at Fordham, The New School, and Catholic University of America (Assistant Professor, 1941).

Allen Wright Thrasher is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed a doctorate under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and studied under traditional teachers V. B. Deo, R. S. Raghavachariar, and K. A. S. Sastri. He worked at the Library of Congress around 1986.
Allison Busch (1969–2020) was an Indology scholar who studied under Sheldon Pollock. She served as Associate Professor of Hindi Literature at Columbia University (attested 2026).
Alnis Dickson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Dickson earned an MA at McGill University (attested 2009) under supervisor Lara Braitstein and also studied under G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Alois Anton Führer (1853–1930) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under Julius Jolly at Würzburg (Ph.D. 1879) and Georg Bühler. His posts included Professor at St. Xavier's, Lucknow Museum Curator, and Archaeological Surveyor in the ASI (c. 1885–1898).

Alois Closs (1893–1984) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He studied at Graz and Vienna under Hans Reichelt, Bernhard Geiger, and others, later serving as Religionsprofessor at Graz Gymnasium (1921–1941) and Steiermärkische Landesbibliothek librarian (1941–1958).

Alois Müller (1835–1901) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He held positions at Palacký University Olomouc (1874–1879), Vienna University Library, and Graz University Library, where he became Director in 1879.

Alois Vaníček (1825–1883) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University (1843–1847) and under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He became Professor of Comparative Literature and Sanskrit at Charles University in 1882.

Alois Walde (1869–1924) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Innsbruck and Leipzig under Friedrich Stolz, Karl Brugmann, and August Leskien. He served as Professor of Comparative Linguistics at Giessen (1909–1912), Innsbruck (1912), and Königsberg (1922–1924).

Aloysius Pieris is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar with degrees from London, Southern Italy, Sri Lanka, and Tilburg, who studied under Bernard de Give. In 1974, he founded and directed the Tulana Research Centre for Encounter and Dialogue.

Alphonse François Lacroix (1799–1859) worked in linguistics and religious studies. He served as an agent for the Netherlands Missionary Society (1821), joined the London Missionary Society (1825), and founded the Bhowanipore Missionary Institution in 1851.
Alubomulle Sumanasara is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Komazawa University from around 1980 to 1985 under the supervision of Yasuaki Nara.
Alva Noë is a philosopher who studied at Oxford (c. 1986–1989) and Harvard (c. 1989–1995). He held faculty posts at UC Santa Cruz (c. 1995–2003) and UC Berkeley (from c. 2003), as well as at CUNY.

Alvan Clark Eastman (1894–1959) worked in Indology and art history after studying at Harvard and NYU. He served as an Oriental art curator at the Detroit Institute of Arts and directed the Evansville Museum, Pasadena Art Institute, and Winnipeg Art Gallery.

Alvappillai Veluppillai (1936–2015) was a scholar of Indology, religion, and linguistics. Educated at Ceylon and Oxford under K. Kanapathypillai and Thomas Burrow, he held posts at Peradeniya, Jaffna, Uppsala (1990–2000), and Arizona State University (2002–2009).
